target.title: fix(cron): batch pending-media snapshot in session reaper to avoid O(SxT) loop
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105694

Fixes an O(S × T) CPU bottleneck in the cron session reaper. For every cron continuation row, `sweepCronRunSessions` called `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey`, which clones and sorts the full task registry. With thousands of sessions, this synchronous work blocks the event loop, causing gateway timeout / WebSocket disconnection.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Instead of repeating per-row task scans, a batch snapshot collects all session keys with pending generated-media work in one pass:

1. **`buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet()`** — one-time scan over task registry + in-process activity map, returns `Set<string>`
2. **Lazy initialization** — snapshot is built only when the first `cronRunContinuation` row is encountered. Idle sweeps (deployments with no cron jobs) pay zero cost and have no task-store failure dependency.
3. **O(1) lookup** — `Set.has()` inside the loop replaces O(T) scan per row

The snapshot preserves the exact `requesterSessionKey` / `ownerKey` matching contract — no semantic change.

#### User Impact

No visible impact. The cron reaper produces identical pruning decisions with strictly less CPU time per sweep.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes
- **Tests:**
  - `task-status-access.test.ts` — 9 tests (+6 for `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet`)
  - `session-reaper.test.ts` — 20 tests (mock updated, pending-media tests use `buildPendingSet`)
  - `cron-run-continuation-cleanup.test.ts` — 5 tests (no regression)
- **Change scope:** 5 files, +131 −5 lines
  - `src/tasks/generated-media-task-activity.ts` — `getAllActiveGeneratedMediaSessionKeys()`
  - `src/tasks/task-status-access.ts` — `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet()`
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.ts` — lazy snapshot + O(1) lookup
  - No config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface

- **Performance:** O(S × T) → O(T + S), real simulation shows 27.2x speedup at 500 sessions × 1000 tasks:

```
[Case 2] Performance scaling — O(S×T) vs O(T+S)
  scale: 500 sessions × 1000 tasks
  old: 13.6ms — 500 full task-list scans (clone+sort each)
  new: 0.5ms — 1 full task-list scan + 500 Set.has() lookups
  speedup: 27.2x
  real clone cost: old=500,000 element copies → new=1,000 element copies
```

- **Real gateway log output** — production `sweepCronRunSessions` with gateway pino-style log:

```
[gateway] INFO  cron-reaper: pruned 2 expired cron run session(s)  {"pruned":2,"retentionMs":86400000}
```

The proof seeds 5 sessions (3 cron run, 2 expired) into a real session store, runs the reaper at `force: true`, and captures the same log format a production gateway emits. After pruning, only the base + recent + regular sessions remain. A second sweep correctly produces no log (pruned=0).

- **Lazy snapshot contract:**
  - 0 continuations → 0 task registry scans (idle sweep fast path)
  - 1+ continuations → 1 scan, all rows use `Set.has()`
  - Test: 5 continuations → 0 per-row `hasPending` calls, batch set populated once

- **[P2] Idle sweep regression fixed** — snapshot is `??=` initialized on first continuation row:

```typescript
let pendingMediaSessionKeys: Set<string> | undefined;
for (const { sessionKey, entry } of listSessionEntries({ storePath })) {
  // ... non-cron-run skip, non-continuation expiry ...
  const continuation = entry.cronRunContinuation;
  if (continuation) {
    pendingMediaSessionKeys ??= buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet();
    if (pendingMediaSessionKeys.has(sessionKey)) continue;
  }
  // ... prune logic ...
}
```
